#!/usr/bin/env python3
from pwn import *
import struct
import os

def create_package(size1=0xC0, size2=0x5, size3=0x80, size4=0x5, magic=b'\x7fPKG', version=1):
    pkg = bytearray()
    
    # Magic number
    pkg.extend(magic)
    
    # Version
    pkg.extend(p32(version))
    
    # Size fields
    pkg.extend(p32(size1))
    pkg.extend(p32(size2))
    pkg.extend(p32(size3))
    pkg.extend(p32(size4))
    
    # Add some dummy data
    pkg.extend(b'\x00' * 0x20)
    
    # Product ID
    pkg.extend(b'EP0001-CELL_00-000000000000000\x00')
    
    # Pad to match size fields
    while len(pkg) < size1:
        pkg.append(0x41)
    
    return bytes(pkg)

def analyze_header(filename):
    with open(filename, 'rb') as f:
        data = f.read()
        
    magic = data[:4]
    version = struct.unpack('>I', data[4:8])[0]
    size1 = struct.unpack('>I', data[8:12])[0]
    size2 = struct.unpack('>I', data[12:16])[0]
    size3 = struct.unpack('>I', data[16:20])[0]
    size4 = struct.unpack('>I', data[20:24])[0]
    
    print(f"[*] Header Analysis:")
    print(f"    Magic: {magic}")
    print(f"    Version: {version}")
    print(f"    Size1: 0x{size1:x} ({size1})")
    print(f"    Size2: 0x{size2:x} ({size2})")
    print(f"    Size3: 0x{size3:x} ({size3})")
    print(f"    Size4: 0x{size4:x} ({size4})")
    
    # Look for patterns in the data
    print("\n[*] Size Relationships:")
    print(f"    Size1 - Size3 = {size1 - size3}")
    print(f"    Size2 - Size4 = {size2 - size4}")
    print(f"    Size1 / Size3 = {size1 / size3:.2f}")
    print(f"    Size2 / Size4 = {size2 / size4:.2f}")

def test_size_relationships():
    print("[*] Testing size field relationships...")
    
    # Original values
    print("\n[*] Original package analysis:")
    analyze_header("cell.pkg")
    
    # Test cases focusing on buffer boundaries
    test_cases = [
        (0x80, 0x5, 0x40, 0x5),  # Half sizes
        (0xC0, 0x7, 0x80, 0x5),  # Modified size2
        (0xC0, 0x5, 0x80, 0x7),  # Modified size4
        (0x100, 0x5, 0x80, 0x5), # Larger size1
        (0xC0, 0x5, 0x100, 0x5), # Larger size3
        (0x7F, 0x5, 0x80, 0x5),  # size1 < 0x80
        (0xC0, 0x5, 0x7F, 0x5),  # size3 < 0x80
        (0xFF, 0x5, 0x80, 0x5),  # size1 near boundary
        (0xC0, 0x5, 0xFF, 0x5),  # size3 near boundary
    ]
    
    for i, (s1, s2, s3, s4) in enumerate(test_cases):
        print(f"\n[*] Test case {i+1}:")
        test_pkg = create_package(s1, s2, s3, s4)
        with open(f"test_pkg_{i}.pkg", "wb") as f:
            f.write(test_pkg)
        try:
            os.chmod(f"test_pkg_{i}.pkg", 0o755)
            output = process(f"./test_pkg_{i}.pkg").recvall()
            print(f"[+] Output: {output}")
        except:
            print("[-] Execution failed")
        os.unlink(f"test_pkg_{i}.pkg")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_size_relationships()

from pwn import *
import struct
import os

def create_pkg(size1, size2, size3, size4, product_id):
    # PKG Header (0x7f + "PKG")
    header = b'\x7f\x50\x4b\x47'
    
    # Version (1)
    version = struct.pack('<I', 1)
    
    # Size fields
    s1 = struct.pack('<I', size1)
    s2 = struct.pack('<I', size2)
    s3 = struct.pack('<I', size3)
    s4 = struct.pack('<I', size4)
    
    # Ensure product ID is proper length and pad if needed
    if not product_id:
        product_id = b"EP0001-CELL_00-000000000000000"
    product_id = product_id[:0x20]
    product_id = product_id.ljust(0x20, b'\x00')
    
    # Add some data after header
    data = os.urandom(max(size1, size3))
    
    return header + version + s1 + s2 + s3 + s4 + product_id + data

def test_pkg(pkg_data, test_name):
    print(f"\n[*] Testing {test_name}")
    
    # Save package to file
    test_file = f"test_{test_name}.pkg"
    with open(test_file, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(pkg_data)
    os.chmod(test_file, 0o755)
    
    try:
        # Run the package
        p = process(f"./{test_file}")
        p.recvall(timeout=1)
        p.close()
        print("[+] Package executed successfully")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[-] Package execution failed: {str(e)}")

# Test cases focusing on size fields and buffer overflow
test_cases = [
    # Test case 1: Equal sizes at boundary
    (0x80, 5, 0x80, 5, b"EP0001-CELL_00-000000000000000"),
    
    # Test case 2: Size1 > Size3 at boundary
    (0x81, 5, 0x80, 5, b"EP0001-CELL_00-000000000000000"),
    
    # Test case 3: Size1 < Size3
    (0x7f, 5, 0x80, 5, b"EP0001-CELL_00-000000000000000"),
    
    # Test case 4: Large size difference
    (0x100, 5, 0x80, 5, b"EP0001-CELL_00-000000000000000"),
    
    # Test case 5: Zero sizes
    (0, 5, 0, 5, b"EP0001-CELL_00-000000000000000"),
    
    # Test case 6: Maximum sizes
    (0xffffffff, 5, 0x80, 5, b"EP0001-CELL_00-000000000000000"),
    
    # Test case 7: Size2 > Size4
    (0x80, 6, 0x80, 5, b"EP0001-CELL_00-000000000000000"),
    
    # Test case 8: Original sizes
    (0xc0, 5, 0x80, 5, b"EP0001-CELL_00-000000000000000"),
    
    # Test case 9: Negative size (signed int overflow)
    (0x80000000, 5, 0x80, 5, b"EP0001-CELL_00-000000000000000"),
    
    # Test case 10: Product ID overflow
    (0x80, 5, 0x80, 5, b"A" * 0x40),
]

# Run all test cases
for i, (s1, s2, s3, s4, pid) in enumerate(test_cases):
    pkg = create_pkg(s1, s2, s3, s4, pid)
    test_pkg(pkg, f"case_{i}")

# Special test: Try to overflow size fields with crafted values
overflow_tests = [
    (0x7fffffff, 0x7fffffff, 0x7fffffff, 0x7fffffff),
    (0x80000000, 0x80000000, 0x80000000, 0x80000000),
    (0xffffffff, 0xffffffff, 0xffffffff, 0xffffffff),
]

for i, (s1, s2, s3, s4) in enumerate(overflow_tests):
    pkg = create_pkg(s1, s2, s3, s4, b"EP0001-CELL_00-000000000000000")
    test_pkg(pkg, f"overflow_{i}")
